components.text: When I got to the United States Senate and went on the Judiciary Committee as a young lawyer, I was of the view and had been trained in the view that the only thing that mattered was whether or not a nominee appointed, suggested by the president had a judicial temperament, had not committed a crime of moral turpitude, and was -- had been a good student
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: it didn't take me long -- it was hard to change, but it didn't take me long, but it took about five years for me to realize that the ideology of that judge makes a big difference
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: That's why I led the fight against Judge Bork
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: Had he been on the court, I suspect there would be a lot of changes that I don't like and the American people wouldn't like, including everything from Roe v. Wade to issues relating to civil rights and civil liberties
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: that was one of the intellectual changes that took place in my career as I got a close look at it
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: that's why I was the first chairman of the Judiciary Committee to forthrightly state that it matters what your judicial philosophy is
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: The American people have a right to understand it and to know it
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: But I did change on that, and -- and I'm glad I did
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: there were times when I wanted to zero-base budget, and to cut taxes even more, and I didn't have enough support in order to accomplish that
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: But on the major principle things, no, there hasn't been something that I've had to compromise on, because we've always seemed to find a way to work together
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: Up there in Alaska, what we have done is, with bipartisan efforts, is work together and, again, not caring who gets the credit for what, as we accomplish things up there
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And that's been just a part of the operation that I wanted to participate in
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And that's what we're going to do in Washington, D.C., also, bring in both sides together
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: John McCain is known for doing that, also, in order to get the work done for the American people
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I have been able to work across the aisle on some of the most controversial issues and change my party's mind, as well as Republicans', because I learned a lesson from Mike Mansfield
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: He said, "Joe, understand one thing. Everyone's sent here for a reason, because there's something in them that their folks like. Don't question their motive."
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: I have never since that moment in my first year questioned the motive of another member of the Congress or Senate with whom I've disagreed
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: I've questioned their judgment
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: I think that's why I have the respect I have and have been able to work as well as I've been able to have worked in the United States Senate
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: That's the fundamental change Barack Obama and I will be bring to this party, not questioning other people's motives
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: You do what I did as governor, and you appoint people regardless of party affiliation, Democrats, independents, Republicans
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: You -- you walk the walk; you don't just talk the talk

components.text: even in my own family, it's a very diverse family
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And we have folks of all political persuasion in there

components.text: I've grown up just knowing that, you know, at the end of the day, as long as we're all working together for the greater good, it's going to be OK

components.text: But the policies and the proposals have got to speak for themselves, also
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And, again, voters on November 4th are going to have that choice to either support a ticket that supports policies that create jobs
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: You do that by lowering taxes on American workers and on our businesses
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And you build up infrastructure
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: you rein in government spending
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: you make our -- our nation energy independent
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: Or you support a ticket that supports policies that will kill jobs by increasing taxes
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And that's what the track record shows, is a desire to increase taxes, increase spending, a trillion-dollar spending proposal that's on the table
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: That's going to hurt our country, and saying no to energy independence
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: Clear choices on November 4th
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: This is such an honor for me
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I appreciate, too, Senator Biden, getting to meet you, finally, also, and getting to debate with you
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And I would like more opportunity for this
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I like being able to answer these tough questions without the filter, even, of the mainstream media kind of telling viewers what they've just heard
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I'd rather be able to just speak to the American people like we just did
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And it's so important that the American people know of the choices that they have on November 4th
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I want to assure you that John McCain and I, we're going to fight for America
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: We're going to fight for the middle-class, average, everyday American family like mine
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I've been there
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I know what the hurts are
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: I know what the challenges are
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And, thank God, I know what the joys are, too, of living in America
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: We are so blessed
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And I've always been proud to be an American
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: And so has John McCain
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: We have to fight for our freedoms, also, economic and our national security freedoms
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: It was Ronald Reagan who said that freedom is always just one generation away from extinction
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: We don't pass it to our children in the bloodstream
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: we have to fight for it and protect it, and then hand it to them so that they shall do the same, or we're going to find ourselves spending our sunset years telling our children and our children's children about a time in America, back in the day, when men and women were free
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: We will fight for it
components.speaker: PALIN

components.text: there is only one man in this race who has really ever fought for you, and that's Senator John McCain

components.text: it really was a pleasure getting to meet you

components.text: No one can deny that the last eight years, we've been dug into a very deep hole here at home with regard to our economy, and abroad in terms of our credibility
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: And there's a need for fundamental change in our economic philosophy, as well as our foreign policy
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: And Barack Obama and I don't measure progress toward that change based on whether or not we cut more regulations and how well CEOs are doing, or giving another $4 billion in tax breaks to the Exxon Mobils of the world
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: We measure progress in America based on whether or not someone can pay their mortgage
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: whether or not they can send their kid to college
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: whether or not they're able to, when they send their child, like we have abroad -- or I'm about to, abroad -- and John has as well, I might add -- to fight, that they are the best equipped and they have everything they need

components.text: And when they come home, they're guaranteed that they have the best health care and the best education possible

components.text: A neighborhood like most of you grew up in
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: We believed it, and we did
components.speaker: BIDEN

components.text: That's why Barack Obama and I are running

components.text: to re-establish that certitude in our neighborhoods
components.speaker: BIDEN
